kurz: Sugar draws juice out of cut fruit: within a quarter of an hour it sits in its own syrup and tastes more intense.
bild_im_kopf: Like a dry sponge on a wet surface: it pulls the water over to itself.
was_passiert: Sugar on cut [[w-obst|fruit]] dissolves in its juice. The concentrated sugar solution draws more water out of the cells (osmosis). This creates a syrup, and the fruit softens.
warum_wichtig: Even pale strawberries taste sweeter and juicier this way. The syrup soaks cake layers and sponge.
faustregeln: Don't leave them for hours: otherwise the fruit turns mushy.
A pinch of salt or a splash of acid makes the flavour fruitier.
schritte: Wash, dry and cut the fruit.
Sprinkle with a little sugar, about one tablespoon per 250 g (as a guide), and mix gently.
Add lemon juice, balsamic vinegar or mint if you like.
